info.title: Tributary control-plane API
info.summary: Channels, versions, validation, deploy, rollback, health (part 1); message search, detail and content, reprocess, replay, stats, live events, retention (part 2). Contract tributary.openapi/v0, set 1.8.
info.description: See contracts/openapi/v0/README.md. Authentication: OIDC bearer access tokens validated as a resource server (ADR-009). The data plane never calls this API (invariant 3). No response echoes a request body, a token claim, or a value from a channel document beyond what the caller sent and stored; validation errors report json_path and keyword only (invariant 6). Operations marked x-tributary-phi-content read or re-publish message content: operator and admin only (ADR-009 D14), each one audited to _tb.<env>.audit before any content is read (contracts/audit/v0).

tags.name: deployments
tags.description: What runs in each environment. Publishing goes to _tb.<env>.channels.

tags.name: messages
tags.description: The message browser over the archive (part 2): search, detail, content, reprocess and replay. Metadata for every role; content operator and admin only.

tags.name: observe
tags.description: Channel stats, the live event stream (SSE) and effective archive retention (part 2). Metadata only.

get.summary: Liveness. Depends on nothing outside the process.
Environments this control plane manages, with their management mode.
List channels, newest version number first within name order.

post.summary: Create a channel and its version 1 from an authored document (metadata.version absent).

get.summary: One channel: latest version and what is deployed where.
Version summaries, newest first. No documents.

post.summary: Add an immutable version. The server assigns the next version number and sets metadata.version.

get.summary: One version with its full document. Documents reveal topology (hosts, ports, buckets), so viewer is not granted.

post.summary: Validate a channel document without storing it: channel-spec schema plus control-plane rules.

200.description: A report, whether or not the document is valid.

get.summary: The current deployment record of every channel deployed in this environment.
Deployment history of one channel in one environment, newest first.

post.summary: Deploy a version: publish its document to _tb.<env>.channels. 202: publishing is asynchronous, and data-plane pickup is never awaited.
Republish an earlier version's stored document unchanged, metadata.version included (README 3.3).
Publish a tombstone for the channel (channel-spec README 6).
Search the archive for one channel, newest first, keyset-paginated. Metadata only, never content. POST so that filters never sit in a URL (README 3.10).

get.summary: One message: its event timeline, each destination's status and an index of stored content (no bytes). Metadata only (README 3.11).
The stored content of one stage (received, routed per destination, dlq). PHI: audited before the read, fail closed (README 3.12).

Cache-Control.description: Always no-store: content is never cached by a browser or a proxy.

post.summary: Re-publish the message's original raw record to the same channel's raw under a new deterministic id, tb-parent-id set to the original. Synchronous: 200 after the broker acknowledged (acks=all). README 3.13.

get.summary: Replays of this channel in this environment, newest first. Metadata only.

post.summary: Replay the channel's raw records with a timestamp in [start, end) back into the SAME channel's raw. No other target exists. A per-key channel needs allow_reorder (README 3.14).

200.description: A replay with this replay_id and an identical request already exists and is running or completed; nothing new starts.

202.description: Accepted; the replay runs in the background (status running). A failed replay re-submitted with the same replay_id and body runs again and regenerates the same ids.

get.summary: One replay and its counts. Metadata only.
Event counts, per-destination outcomes and delivery durations, top error codes and the channel versions seen per instance, over a window, from the archive (README 3.15). No consumer lag.

Live message events for up to 16 channels as Server-Sent Events, tailed from the archive (README 3.16). Metadata only. Clients send the bearer header with a fetch-based reader: EventSource cannot, and a query-string token is refused (ADR-009 D1).

200.description: An event stream. Each SSE event has an event name and one line of JSON data; message events carry an id usable as Last-Event-ID.

get.summary: Effective archive retention per store, as the migrate step last applied it (ADR-004 R3, R6). Read-only: there is no write surface in the API.

oidcBearer.description: An access token from the operator's OIDC provider, validated as a resource server (ADR-009 rev 2): signature against the issuer's JWKS, keys selected by kid from a cached key set (jku, x5u, x5c and jwk headers ignored); algorithm allow-list RS256, PS256, ES256; typ at+jwt (JWT only when the operator enables it, and never an ID token); exp, iss, aud and sub required; nbf and iat honoured. Roles come from a configured claim that must be an array of strings, mapped to Tributary roles; an operation is allowed only to the roles in its x-tributary-roles. Authorization header only, sent once: a token in a query string or form body is refused, even alongside a header. The API issues no tokens and keeps no sessions.

MessageIdPath.name: message_id
MessageIdPath.description: tb-msg-id. An engine-minted UUID, never derived from a payload field (envelope/v0).

DestinationQuery.name: destination
DestinationQuery.description: Required with stage=routed; optional with stage=dlq (a loader's dead letter names its destination); refused with stage=received (422 REQUEST_INVALID).

StreamChannelsQuery.name: channel
StreamChannelsQuery.description: Repeat for each channel, 1 to 16. Channel names are not PHI; filters that could be (attributes) are not offered on the stream.

LastEventIdHeader.name: Last-Event-ID
LastEventIdHeader.description: The id of the last message event received; the stream resumes after it if it is at most 15 minutes old, otherwise it sends reset and continues live.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: not JSON, wrong type, bad cursor (REQUEST_INVALID).

Unauthorized.description: No token (AUTH_REQUIRED) or a token that failed validation (TOKEN_INVALID), including a token sent by more than one method, a malformed roles claim, or no usable signing keys. Which check failed is not disclosed.

WWW-Authenticate.description: RFC 6750: Bearer, with error="invalid_token" when a token was sent. Never an error_description built from claims.

Forbidden.description: Valid token, no role that grants this operation (FORBIDDEN).

NotFound.description: Environment, channel, version or replay does not exist (NOT_FOUND); the archive holds no event for this message id in this channel, possibly because the archive lags (MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND); no content is stored for that stage (CONTENT_NOT_FOUND).

Conflict.description: Part 1: CHANNEL_EXISTS, CURRENT_VERSION_MISMATCH, MANAGEMENT_MODE, NOTHING_TO_ROLL_BACK, NOT_DEPLOYED. Part 2: CONTENT_STORAGE_OFF; reprocess and replay refusals ORDERING_WOULD_BREAK, DESTINATION_SCOPED, CHILD_MESSAGE, NO_PAYLOAD_COORDINATES, OFFSET_NOT_FOUND, RECORD_MISMATCH, RECORD_UNDECODABLE, ENVELOPE_INVALID; REQUEST_ID_REUSED (README 3.13-3.14). NOT_DEPLOYED also answers reprocess and replay for a channel not deployed in this environment.

Gone.description: The original raw record is below the topic's log start: Kafka retention lapsed (RETENTION_LAPSED).

TooManyRequests.description: This subject already holds the maximum number of open event streams (TOO_MANY_STREAMS).

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency of this operation is down: ARCHIVE_UNAVAILABLE (ClickHouse), AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE (the audit record could not be committed, so no content was read and nothing was published), SOURCE_ERROR, SOURCE_TIMEOUT (reading raw), PRODUCE_FAILED, PRODUCE_TIMEOUT, PRODUCE_REFUSED (re-publishing to raw; republished says how many the broker acknowledged), UNAVAILABLE. The data plane is unaffected (invariants 3 and 9).

Unprocessable.description: Well-formed but refused: SPEC_INVALID (with errors), VERSION_SET_BY_CLIENT, CHANNEL_NAME_MISMATCH, REQUEST_INVALID (part 2 also: until not after since, end not after start, a destination with stage=received, an identifier-shaped search attribute).

ChannelName.description: metadata.name; same grammar as the topic segment (topics/v0 1).

Version.description: Channel version, assigned by the control plane, becomes metadata.version and tb-channel-version.

Subject.description: The token's sub claim. Staff identity, not PHI; stored for audit, never logged with the token.

Cursor.description: Opaque. Clients must not parse it.

ApiReadiness.description: The component=api case of contracts/observability/v0 readiness.schema.json, which is authoritative.

management_mode.description: ADR-001 6.8. git-managed: deploy and rollback accept only versions whose origin.kind is git.

profile.description: topics/v0 profile. lite is barred from production use (topics/v0 3.8).

ChannelDocument.description: A channel-spec document (contracts/channel-spec/v0/channel.schema.json, the authority). Typed loosely here on purpose: the server validates it against the channel-spec schema and answers 422 SPEC_INVALID; clients that want field types generate them from that schema. On create, metadata.version must be absent.

Origin.description: Where the document came from. Client-asserted: it drives the git-managed rule, it is not a security boundary (RBAC and the audit trail are).

spec_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored document as published (README 3.2).

document.description: As stored and published: metadata.version equals version.

DeploymentStatus.description: pending: accepted, not yet committed to _tb.<env>.channels. published: committed (acks=all); says nothing about which workers have applied it (observe tb_spec_version). failed: the publish did not commit. superseded: a later record in this environment replaced it before it published.

version.description: The version published; null for undeploy (tombstone).

previous_version.description: What was current when this was requested; null when nothing was.

expected_current_version.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard: the version the caller believes is current, null for not deployed. Mismatch: 409 CURRENT_VERSION_MISMATCH. Absent: no check.
Required, so two operators cannot roll back twice by accident.

to_version.description: Default: the most recently published version in this environment that differs from the current one. Repeated default rollbacks therefore alternate between two versions; name to_version to go further back (README 3.3).

ValidationIssue.description: Where and which rule, never the message: a jsonschema message embeds the failing value (contracts/README.md).

validator.description: A JSON Schema keyword, or a control-plane rule name (README 3.4).

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, restricted: no instance member (it would echo the path), detail is fixed text per code, never input.

code.description: Closed list. Part 2 codes (from MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND on) map one-to-one to the tributary-archiver library's refusal and failure codes where one exists (README 4.1).

request_id.description: This HTTP request's id, for support and log correlation. Not a reprocess operation_id.

republished.description: Reprocess failures after the audit requested record only: records the broker acknowledged before the failure. At-least-once: an acknowledged record stays on raw, and a retry with the same operation_id re-publishes the same tb-msg-id.

Uuid7.description: Canonical lowercase UUIDv7 (RFC 9562), the tb-msg-id grammar.

DestinationName.description: A destination name from the channel spec.

RawTopic.description: <env>.<channel>.raw (topics/v0). Reprocess and replay write only to the source channel's own raw.

SearchCursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor of the archive query library (up to 512 characters, longer than the part 1 Cursor). Clients must not parse it.

ContentStage.description: Stages with stored content (ADR-004 A2): received from raw, routed from out.<dest> (per destination), dlq from dlq. Steps inside a pipeline run in process (invariant 2), so there is no separate content for transformed.

AttrName.description: A non-identifying search attribute name: the events/v0 attrs grammar minus the identifier deny-list and minus any *_hmac name. Identifier-derived search is deferred (ADR-004 H3, wave-3.md 2.7 D2).

AttrValue.description: A short code: no spaces, no HL7 delimiters, at most 64 characters (events/v0 attrs).

MessageSearchRequest.description: Filters for one channel (in the path). since is required: with the channel it bounds the scan (query library cost rule). status, error_code and attrs apply after deduplication. All filters AND together.

until.description: Exclusive. Must be after since (422 REQUEST_INVALID).

MessageEvent.description: One deduplicated archived message event (events/v0, kind message), as the query library returns it. Metadata only: no payload, no key, no tb-usr-* value, and no *_hmac attribute.

ClaimCheckLocator.description: Opaque locator, the tb-claim-check grammar: no query string, no fragment, no userinfo, so never a presigned URL (a stored, replayable credential).

DestinationStatus.description: Where one destination stands for this message: the stage of its newest event. A destination the message was never routed to does not appear.

attempt.description: Highest tb-attempt seen for this destination.

ContentRef.description: Index entry for one stored content row. Sizes and types only, never bytes.

MessageDetail.description: Exit criterion 1's response, without content: the timeline, each destination's status and the content index. Content is read per stage through getMessageContent (operator, admin; audited).

events.description: Oldest first, one per (stage, destination, attempt); a re-emitted event keeps its original place.

truncated.description: true when the timeline hit the 1000-row cap.

content.description: Empty when content storage is off (TB_ARCHIVE_CONTENT, ADR-004 A4) or nothing is stored yet.

MessageContent.description: PHI. One stored content row. Inline payloads are base64 of the exact bytes the stage committed (invariant 8: opaque bytes). Claim-checked payloads return the locator only; fetching the object through the API is not in v0 (README 6).

payload_base64.description: RFC 4648 base64 of at most 1048576 bytes (the envelope's inline limit).

headers.description: The envelope headers stored with the content (ADR-004 A2). Never tb-usr-* or tb-x-*.

operation_id.description: Minted by the client once per operator action and reused on every retry of it. Passed to the library as request_id. The new tb-msg-id is a deterministic function of (message_id, operation_id) (README 3.13), so a retry re-publishes the SAME id and loader idempotency absorbs it (invariant 4).

allow_reorder.description: Required true on a channel with ordering per-key, or the request is refused 409 ORDERING_WOULD_BREAK (invariant 5). Recorded in the audit requested record.

new_message_id.description: tb-msg-id of the re-published record; its tb-parent-id is original_message_id.

ReplayRequest.description: No target field exists: replay writes only to the source channel's own raw (lead's ruling 2026-10-06, wave-3.md 2.6 H8), and strict producers refuse an unknown field.

replay_id.description: Minted by the client once per operator action. Each republished record gets tb-msg-id = f(original id, replay_id), so a re-run regenerates the same ids.

start.description: Inclusive, on the Kafka record timestamp.

end.description: Exclusive. Must be after start (422 REQUEST_INVALID).

allow_reorder.description: Required true on a channel with ordering per-key (409 ORDERING_WOULD_BREAK otherwise). Recorded in the audit requested record.

max_records.description: Upper bound on the offset span; a larger span fails the replay with RANGE_TOO_LARGE before anything is published.

ReplayFailureCode.description: Why a running replay stopped. The library's ReplayRefused and PublishError codes after the audit requested record, plus INTERRUPTED (the API process stopped while it ran; reported once deadline_at has passed) and INTERNAL.

span.description: Upper bound of the offset span read (includes control records and out-of-range timestamps).

republished.description: Records the broker acknowledged. On failed, the partial count: those records stay on raw (at-least-once).

ChannelStats.description: Computed from the archive over [since, until). Counts are deduplicated EVENTS, not messages: a message routed to two destinations adds two routed and up to two sent. The archive lags the data plane by the archiver's batch delay. No consumer lag: the API holds no Kafka grant to read it (Prometheus and KEDA have it, observability/v0).

duration_ms_p50.description: Of duration_ms on sent events; null when there were none.

errors.description: Top error codes by count, descending.

versions.description: Channel versions stamped on events in the window, with the number of distinct instances that stamped each. This is how an operator sees a deploy or rollback applied (README 3.4).

StreamNotice.description: data of reset (cursor_expired, cursor_invalid, backlog_too_dense: the stream continues live from now, and events between the last id and now were NOT sent; use search to fill the gap) and end (token_expiring, max_duration, server_shutdown: the server closes the stream; reconnect with a fresh token and Last-Event-ID).

RetentionSettings.description: From the archive_settings table the migrate step writes (ADR-004 R6). A store with no row has never been migrated, or is content with TB_ARCHIVE_CONTENT off. Kafka topic retention is not here: it is not a records-retention control (ADR-004 R8).

store.description: events: message_events (TB_ARCHIVE_TTL_DAYS); content: message_content (TB_ARCHIVE_CONTENT_TTL_DAYS); audit: audit_log (TB_ARCHIVE_AUDIT_TTL_DAYS).

release.description: The release that applied it, as the migrate step recorded it.
